notes: Cross-verse split with MRK.15.3 in the ASV's 'accuse X of Y' frame. Both verses render κατηγορέω with a genitive of the person and an accusative of the thing; 15.3 puts the English 'of' on the accusative of the thing (πολλά -> 'of many things') and leaves the genitive person a bare 'him'. 15.4 put the same frame's 'of' on the genitive person (σου -> 'thee of'), treating it as a case preposition. It is not one: were 'of' the genitive's own realization, 15.3 would read 'accused of him'. The only thing that differs between the verses is that the ASV strands 'of' at the end of the English clause at 15.4, and rules 53 and 63 forbid reading a helper off English word order while rule 15 permits the discontinuity. The 'of' therefore goes to πόσα, the token realizing the thing accused of, and σου stands on a bare 'thee'.
